quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if they cross against a red light or cross carelessly.

questions.question: Vehicle stopping distance never depends on:

options.text: The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These make roads slippery. Safety may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or horns with red or blue flashing lights. Follow instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Do not use the brakes right away.
Gradually slow down and pull to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, release the gas pedal and do not apply the brakes immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, you should look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, you may pass if:
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line in the center, and the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It tells drivers what they must obey. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, the driver of a small vehicle should be prepared for:

options.text: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: When you see a school bus on the opposite side of a two-lane road, you must stop if:

options.text: The red warning lights are flashing.
The bus is off the road and the yellow lights are flashing.
The bus has flashing yellow lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: The red warning lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with red flashing lights on either side of a two-lane road. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a road with three or more lanes, or if there is a median or barrier between you and the bus.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks right away as fast as you can.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to let any train pass first.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to let any train pass first.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to let trains pass before you cross the tracks. Wait until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks before crossing. Do not change gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed to use:

options.text: The full lane width like other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane width, just like all other vehicles on the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and stay at a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and stay at a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency braking. Emergency stops can cause the driver behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive with caution.

questions.question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles have:
questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger its blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights on, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights to warn them.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If headlights are blinding you, look away from them and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This will protect your vision.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking on the road ahead.
Construction workers are on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is coming. Drive carefully where pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights, what should you do?

options.text: Approach with great care and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only cross when a flagger tells you it is safe.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with great care and only cross when you are sure no train is coming from any direction. Follow all instructions from a flagger if one is present at the crossing.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Use your horn to warn other drivers that you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge smoothly with traffic.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When you enter a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.question: Which of the following helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted in the middle of lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the middle of lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than what is reasonable and safe. Adjust your speed based on traffic, weather, road conditions, pedestrians, and light. Always obey posted speed limits.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bicycle lanes and a cyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. It is the cyclist's responsibility to move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would any other vehicle, but carefully and at a safe distance. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of cyclists. Do not honk, as it may startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.
